_readme: Hand labels for measuring the judge. Score a run yourself against the same rubric in eval/judge.ts, then record only the criteria you actually checked. Five runs is enough to be worth reporting. Criterion ids: risk_band, contradictions, no_recommendation, no_fabrication, evidence_complete.

_example.note: Agent named no product. All figures traceable.

labels.note: no_fabrication: client said 'long term, whatever' — dismissive, not firmly established — and the agent restated it as a settled fact ('you've said long-term, which is good') without re-confirming. communicated_band: client gave essentially no real answers (no amount, no firm horizon), and the agent still told him he was in a 'higher risk band' and listed eligible categories. Both count as real failures on independent read.

Agrees with the run's overall fail, but for a mixed reason: the stated-risk-vs-behavioural pair the agent logged is a FALSE POSITIVE on independent read — holding through a drop while wanting to actively hedge/rebalance is not actually contradictory, the agent was too aggressive calling it one. The knowledge-vs-demonstrated pair (ETFs are not 'capital protected'; multiple funds on the same index isn't diversification) IS a genuine, correctly-caught contradiction. Net: agent found the real one and manufactured an extra one, so the criterion is correctly failed, but not for the reason the terse 'spurious' label implies.

DISAGREES WITH SCORER, NOT THE AGENT. Fixture's expected_risk_band is 2; agent computed 1. On independent transcript read, band 1 is the stronger read of her actual words: 'quite anxious' about a 10% drop, explicitly says she 'couldn't leave it alone' and would 'pull it out before things got worse,' wants 'something stable.' That is closer to capital-preservation behaviour than cautious-with-some-tolerance. Recommend revisiting fixtures/personas/13-ivana-wedding.json's expected_risk_band — may be a ground-truth error, not a model/policy failure. Separately, expected_capacity_for_loss (medium) does look right against the agent's actual read (high) — an emergency fund and stable income don't offset that this is money for a fixed, near-term purpose.
